title: Customer feedback bridge and unscoped feature bundles - Dec 2026
summary: Working synthesis of recent customer signals about latency/cost tradeoffs, grouped into three unscoped feature bundles we can propose as quick experiments or sales plays. Notes are intentionally rough — capture of a 2026-12-03 cross-functional readout + post-meeting refinement.
body:
Context and why this doc exists:
- Post-holiday surge in inbound runtime asks from mid-market customers. Many notes in CS about latency spikes for conversational flows and requests for finer-grained cost controls.
- This doc is a synthesis attempt to avoid repeating identical asks into separate tickets: cluster asks, propose unscoped bundles, and define quick experiments that engineering + solutions can run with.

High-level synthesis (raw themes):
1) Prefix/KV cache discoverability and controls: customers want clearer visibility into what is being cached, TTL controls per-project, and a simple UI/API to flush/inspect cached prefixes. Several also ask for a lighter-weight 'session cache' for chat apps.
2) Cost-aware routing and model transparency: requests for auto-routing to cheaper quantized variants when under cost thresholds, plus clearer per-request cost estimation before committing a run.
3) Fine-grained throttles and per-route batching knobs: customers (platform teams) want the ability to pin batch windows per-route or set min-latency budgets so that the runtime doesn't batch aggressively for latency-sensitive endpoints.
4) Operator tooling for KV cache regressions: when cache invalidation occurs (user-reported), SRE and CS both struggle to debug whether regressions are model changes, compiler/kernel swaps, or cache misses.

Representative customer asks (anonymized snippets):
- "We need to see which user prefixes are being cached and set 10s TTLs for certain flows — we can't have full-session caching for short-lived tokens." (YC startup, chat features)
- "If traffic spikes we want to route to cheaper quantized model with slightly higher latency but lower cost — toggleable per-customer." (SaaS enterprise)
- "Our payment flow times out when a background batch packs tokens — can we guarantee a max-p99 latency by route?" (fintech)
- "When we see hallucination regressions after an infra change, we want a map of affected cache keys and trace ids to reproduce locally." (marketplace)

Clustered feature requests (unscoped bundles):
Bundle A: Cache observability + lightweight controls (low engineering risk)
- Features: cache inspector API (list prefixes + hit/miss stats), per-project TTL override, session-cache mode (ephemeral, per-conversation), cache-flush endpoint.
- Rationale: repeatedly requested, high perceived value, low infra risk. Low-to-medium cost to implement as a layered API + small Console additions.
- Quick experiment: ship an internal-only API prototype and instrument 3 pilot customers with CS support for 4 weeks.

Bundle B: Cost-aware model routing + preflight cost estimate (medium risk)
- Features: server-side routing policy (route-by-cost threshold), per-request cost-estimator (estimated tokens * model-cost), default fallback to quantized variants under budget. Admin UI toggle for customers.
- Rationale: Requests appear in sales conversations as a major blocker for adoption in fintech and education. Implementation touches routing and billing pipeline (requires simulation runway).
- Quick experiment: enable in a dedicated pool where we can A/B route 10% of calls to quantized variants and compare cost + quality.

Bundle C: Per-route latency SLO knobs + batching profiles (higher risk, complex ergonomics)
- Features: per-route min-batch windows, SLO-based batching policy, p99 enforcement with automatic fallback to single-request execution, telemetry panel for batching metrics.
- Rationale: Some customers are willing to trade cost for firm latency guarantees; this is an enterprise upsell and requires SRE guardrails.
- Quick experiment: add a per-route flag that disables batching for a route (boolean) and test with two pilot customers before building fine-grained windows.

Operational and SRE probes (cross-cutting):
- Unified trace linking: for any cached response include cache-key metadata in trace/span so SRE/CS can reconstruct sequences.
- Regression triage playbook: a short-runbook for CS->SRE->Eng triage that includes which traces to capture, suggested queries, and a provable repro path.
- Synthetic traffic probes that simulate prefix patterns customers use (for early detection of cache warmup/regen failures).

Prioritization heuristics suggested here (for discussion):
- Customer impact score = (#customers requesting * ARR bucket weight) + severity (latency outage vs feature request).
- Engineering effort estimate (T-shirt) and risk (runtime stability, billing changes).
- Time-to-learn: prioritize experiments that give clear telemetry within 2–4 weeks.

Unresolved questions we should decide before scoping:
- How much exposure do we want in Console vs API-first approach? Many POCs ask for Console toggles, but API-first scales better for automation.
- Billing integration: do we surface preflight cost estimates on the hosted API before billing change? This requires alignment with billing teams.
- Security/compliance: session-cache mode may inadvertently store PII — require KMS/HSM hooks or opt-out by default.

Short-term next steps (owner assignments):
- Priya: synthesize pilot-candidate customer list (due 2026-12-10) and share with Solutions.
- Ethan: prototype Cache Inspector API (internal) and wire basic metrics (due 2026-12-17).
- Marta: write CS triage runbook draft (due 2026-12-14) and coordinate a dry-run with SRE.
- Liam: scope the per-route batching disable flag experiment and estimate infra changes (due 2026-12-20).

Communication and outbound notes:
- Sales play: bundle B is the best lead-in for enterprise deals where cost predictability is a procurement blocker. Prepare a 2-slide appendix showing cost delta and rollback story.
- Internal comms: post a short note to #product-optimize summarizing the pilot program and inviting participants. Use code "cache-bridge" in subject.

Appendix: quick signals and data (raw):
- 11 inbound CS threads (Nov-Dec 2026) referencing cache/ttl/visibility.
- 6 enterprise RFIs asking for cost routing.
- Pilot candidates flagged: Acme Fintech (high ARR), Tutorly (mid ARR, many short chat sessions), RetailOps (low ARR but heavy burst traffic).

Immediate risks to flag:
- Exposing cache internals could be misinterpreted by customers and create support burden. Need good defaults and helpful docs.
- Routing to quantized variants may expose quality regressions; require eval sets and automated quality checks as part of rollout.

Questions for the next cross-functional readout (2026-12-15):
- Decide whether to prioritize Bundle A (low friction) or Bundle B (enterprise sales lift).
- Confirm a pilot customer roster and CS engagement model.
- Agree a minimal observability contract that must ship with each bundle.

Notes-to-self / loose ideas (scratch):
- Consider a "cache preview" view in Console that shows example completions for cached prefixes to help customers reason about cache TTLs.
- Could we add a per-request header to opt into cheaper routing (like X-Redwood-CostHint: low)? Might be an easy backward-compatible hook for partners.

End of draft.

If you read this and have flagged customer names we should recruit for pilots, add them to the Confluence page and drop a note in the shared thread.
